note: Adjudicated 8-byte magic collisions: one wire value claimed by two or more distinct constant names, where the sharing has been examined and found safe. The gate (`dclutch-route-census inventory --check-unique`, see tools/gauntlet/census/src/magics.rs) fails on every collision that is NOT listed here, so a genuinely new one still stops the build. This file is a register of positive facts, not a mute switch. Three rules make it one. (1) Every entry MUST carry a `verdict` that names the specific reason THIS sharing cannot mis-dispatch; an entry without an argued verdict is refused by the gate, because an exemption that records nothing is a hidden failure -- which is the whole defect class this instrument exists to find. (2) `constants` must list the EXACT set of names observed at the magic. If a third constant later claims a listed value, the set no longer matches and the collision fires again -- so an exemption pins a fact, it does not silence a value. (3) An entry whose magic no longer collides is reported as stale and must be deleted, exactly as tools/gauntlet/blocked.json entries are. The safety question is always the same: can ONE dispatcher see both constants? Different ELFs never meet a single dispatcher. A request paired with a receipt never meets one either -- instruction data and account data are different channels. Same-ELF sharing is a hazard and does not belong in this file; DCLTDRS1 was re-lettered (b64ecbb5) rather than exempted, and DCLTRIX1 is here only because its partition is now enforced by compile-time assertions rather than by prose. Adjudicated 2026-09-01 by lane S11; see docs/evidence/DEBT_OWNERSHIP_LEDGER_2026_09_01.md section 2.4.1.

exempt.verdict: SAME-ELF, and safe only because the split is now MECHANICAL. The Registry ELF dispatches both RECORD_INSTRUCTION_MAGIC_V1 and REGISTRY_INSTRUCTION_MAGIC_V1; they are partitioned by the action byte at offset 10, Registry owning 0..=REGISTRY_ACTION_CEILING_V1 and the record family owning RECORD_FIRST_ACTION_V1 upward. That rule was documented but FALSE until 2026-09-01 -- RecordActionV1::Begin was action 1, inside Registry's half beside Reauthenticate = 1, and the only thing keeping a Record Begin from executing as a Registry Reauthenticate was the dispatcher's length clause plus the arithmetic accident that BEGIN_RECORD_BYTES_V1 is 176 and REGISTRY_INSTRUCTION_BYTES_V1 is 16. Both sides were valid traffic of their own family, which is what made it worse than a decode collision. Begin is now 5, and two `const _: () = assert!` in programs/dclutch-registry-sbf/src/lib.rs bind the ranges disjoint and the widths distinct; crates/dclutch-registry-svm/src/tests.rs proves the ceiling is what decode actually admits, and crates/dclutch-record-contract/src/lib.rs asserts every record action sits at or above the boundary. RELAY_INSTRUCTION_MAGIC is dispatched by dclutch-resolution-proof-sbf, a different ELF, so it never meets either. Delete this entry if those assertions ever go.

NOT A DISPATCH SELECTOR. This is the LiabilityBasisV2 aggregate ACCOUNT header, read when decoding account data, never compared against instruction data -- no dispatcher of any ELF sees it. The three names are one canonical constant (crates/dclutch-claims-svm/src/liability_basis_state_v2.rs) plus two program-test fixtures that re-declare the same value locally instead of importing it. Harmless to dispatch, still worth fixing: the fixtures should import the canonical constant so the record has one author. Tracked as a convergence item, not a safety one.

NOT A DISPATCH SELECTOR, and the exact sibling of DCLLBM02: the LiabilityBasisV2 Position ACCOUNT header, read from account data only. One canonical declaration plus two program-test fixtures re-declaring the same value under local names. No dispatcher compares it against instruction data, so no mis-routing is possible; the fixtures should import the canonical constant.

DIFFERENT ELFS AND DIFFERENT CHANNELS. AGGREGATE_RETIREMENT_FINISH_MAGIC_V1 belongs to the Core retirement checkpoint (crates/dclutch-market-core-codec), ARTIFACT_RELEASE_MAGIC_V1 to the Registry artifact record (crates/dclutch-registry-contract). No single program dispatches on both, and neither is an instruction selector reached from the other's entrypoint. A reader of a raw wire dump can still confuse them, which is why this is recorded rather than dismissed.

REQUEST PAIRED WITH RECEIPT, different channels. DIRECT_ACTIVATION_REQUEST_MAGIC_V1 heads an instruction; DEALER_SCENARIO_ACTIVATION_RECEIPT_MAGIC_V1 heads a receipt read back from account data. A receipt magic is never tested against instruction_data by any dispatcher, so the two cannot select each other's handler.

ONE DISPATCH SELECTOR, ONE RECORD, inside the same family. The commit magic is a top-level Trading selector (is_dealer_scenario_checkpoint_commit_v1); the custody-effect manifest magic heads persisted account data and is never compared against instruction_data. Only one of the two is ever reachable from a dispatcher, so there is no arm for the other to be mistaken for. Note this is the closest of the eight to a real hazard: if the manifest ever became instruction-carried inside the Trading ELF, this entry must be deleted and the magic re-lettered.

TWO RECEIPTS, neither a dispatch selector. Both head data read back and authenticated against an expected magic the reader already knows from context -- the reader is looking for one specific receipt, not choosing between families. No dispatcher compares either against instruction_data, so no wrong-handler path exists.

DIFFERENT ELFS. ADMISSION_REQUEST_MAGIC_V2 is the Product Runtime V2 admission request (crates/dclutch-product-runtime-v2-admission, dispatched by dclutch-product-runtime-v2-sbf); PAYOFF_REQUEST_MAGIC_V2 is the payoff request of crates/dclutch-product-payoff-v2-svm. Neither program's entrypoint sees the other's constant, so one dispatcher never has to choose. Both are genuine request magics, which makes this the one to re-letter first -- but NOT YET. HELD 2026-09-01 until the current devnet cohort reports live: the deploy lane is rebuilding its ELF pack at a post-adjudication commit, and moving a magic mid-rebuild would leave it deploying artifacts that no longer match its recorded hashes. There is no hazard in waiting, because the two constants are in different ELFs and no dispatcher chooses between them. Ember's deploy grant is standing ("as often as you feel ready"), so the next redeploy is cheap and this belongs to it. Land it after the cohort is live, not before.

AN ACK AND A RECEIPT, neither a dispatch selector. SHADOW_ACK_MAGIC_V3 heads return data from the shadow accelerator; TERMINAL_SETTLEMENT_RECEIPT_MAGIC_V3 heads a Claims settlement receipt. Both are verified by a caller that already knows which one it asked for, and neither is compared against instruction_data at any entrypoint.
